From 8cd2942e354687b6f655ef831d5d525d63dd46a8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Varun Thacker <varun@apache.org>
Date: Thu, 3 Aug 2017 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] SOLR-11182: A split shard failure on IOException should be
 logged


diff --git a/solr/CHANGES.txt b/solr/CHANGES.txt
index be89d0632ee..012ac868224 100644
--- a/solr/CHANGES.txt
+++ b/solr/CHANGES.txt
@@ -420,6 +420,8 @@ Bug Fixes
 * SOLR-11163: Fix contrib/ltr Normalizer persistence after solr core reload or restart.
   (Yuki Yano via Christine Poerschke)
 
+* SOLR-11182: A split shard failure on IOException should be logged (Varun Thacker)
+
 Optimizations
 ----------------------
 

diff --git a/solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/update/DirectUpdateHandler2.java b/solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/update/DirectUpdateHandler2.java
index 3efb748fd02..bfed1c17d9a 100644
--- a/solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/update/DirectUpdateHandler2.java
+++ b/solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/update/DirectUpdateHandler2.java
@@ -911,6 +911,7 @@ public class DirectUpdateHandler2 extends UpdateHandler implements SolrCoreState
     } catch (IOException e) {
       numErrors.increment();
       numErrorsCumulative.mark();
+      throw e;
     }
   }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications Summary

#### 1. Modifications in Each File:
- **`solr/CHANGES.txt`**:
  - Added a new entry under "Bug Fixes" to document the fix related to SOLR-11182, stating that a split shard failure on IOException should be logged. The entry includes the contributor's name (Varun Thacker).

- **`solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/update/DirectUpdateHandler2.java`**:
  - In the catch block for IOException, a new line was added to rethrow the caught IOException (`throw e;`). This modification ensures that the IOException is propagated up the call stack.

#### 2. Relationships:
The changes in `DirectUpdateHandler2.java` are directly related to the logging enhancement mentioned in `CHANGES.txt`. By modifying the exception handling to rethrow the IOException, the patch ensures that failures related to split shards are not silently ignored; instead, they can be logged by higher-level error handling mechanisms. This aligns with the intent of SOLR-11182 to improve error visibility during shard operations.
